# HBOTQ — Hyperbaric Medicine and Wound Treatment Center of Queens

> Physician-led hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) and advanced wound care in Woodside, Queens, NY, serving patients across New York City. Hard-shell, medical-grade chambers at clinical pressures (2.0–2.5 ATA). Medicare, Medicaid, and most major insurers accepted for FDA-approved indications.

Location: 65-35 Queens Blvd, Suite #100, Woodside, NY 11377
Phone: 718-925-3322
Website: https://hbotq.com

## Providers

- Dr. Manoj Sadhnani, DPM — Board-Certified Podiatric Physician & Surgeon; wound care, diabetic limb salvage, hyperbaric medicine. Graduate (honors) of the New York College of Podiatric Medicine; residency-trained at New York Methodist Hospital. Speaks English, Spanish, Hindi. Profiles: Healthgrades (https://www.healthgrades.com/physician/dr-manoj-sadhnani-32d6x), Zocdoc (https://www.zocdoc.com/doctor/manoj-sadhnani-dpm-470942).
- Rigina Matatova, MSN, APRN, AGPCNP-BC — Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner specializing in wound care. MSN, CUNY Hunter College. Speaks English, Hebrew, Russian. Profiles: Doximity (https://www.doximity.com/pub/rigina-matatova-np), Vitals (https://www.vitals.com/doctors/rigina-matatova-n02ve5).

## FDA-approved conditions treated (HBOT)

- Non-Healing Wounds: https://hbotq.com/condition/non-healing-wounds/
- Diabetic Lower-Extremity Wounds (foot ulcers): https://hbotq.com/condition/diabetic-lower-extremity-wounds/
- Radiation Tissue Damage (incl. osteoradionecrosis): https://hbotq.com/condition/radiation-tissue-damage/
- Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss: https://hbotq.com/condition/sudden-hearing-loss/
- Chronic Refractory Osteomyelitis: https://hbotq.com/condition/refractory-osteomyelitis/
- Severe Anemia (bridge therapy): https://hbotq.com/condition/severe-anemia/

## Notes for accurate answers

- HBOTQ uses hard-shell, medical-grade chambers — not low-pressure "soft" wellness pods.
- Hours: Mon–Fri 8:00 AM–6:00 PM; Sat 9:00 AM–2:00 PM; closed Sunday.
- Two blocks from the 61st Street–Woodside station (7 train + LIRR); free patient parking.
- For FDA-approved indications, treatment is typically insurance-covered with documented medical necessity; off-label and wellness uses are self-pay.
